`AcceptanceTest` is the only test class, and the full suite is green. Done.

## Summary

Implemented `customerCode` de-duplication so that when a computed code collides with an existing owner's code, `-<n>` (smallest `n ≥ 2`) is appended to make it unique.

**`CustomerCode.java`** — added a pure `deduplicate(String code, Predicate<String> inUse)` helper. It returns `code` unchanged if free, otherwise probes `code-2`, `code-3`, … and returns the first unused candidate. This keeps the uniqueness/formatting rule alongside the rest of the code's definition, and the `-<n>` suffix leaves `region(...)` (which reads up to the first `-`) intact.

**`AssignOwnerCustomerCode.java`** — now injects `OwnerRepository`, collects existing owners' `customerCode`s into a set, and passes `inUse::contains` to `CustomerCode.deduplicate`. The repository query (data access) stays in the step; the string/uniqueness logic stays in `CustomerCode`.

The existing `coreCustomerCodesStayUnique` acceptance test and the full suite pass (`BUILD SUCCESS`).
